# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

## Plan (plan_complete)

Decomposed into 8 child work items (test-first / vertical-slice), all at
stage `intake_complete`:

**Phase 1 — Foundation**
- Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock module (AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ)

**Phase 2 — Grid + invariant**
- Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG)
- Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing (AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**
- Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A)
- Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire (AH-0MUGY7ZUO008QSUX)

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**
- Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ)
- Update documentation: GDD sections, README, code comments (AH-0MUGY8DPC005ERM9)
- Run full test suite and fix any failures (AH-0MUGY8HHU006XMU9)

**Dependency edges:** T2→T1, T3→T1, T4→T3, T5→{T1,T2}, T6→T4,
T7→{T2,T3,T4,T5}, T8→{T6,T7}.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every implementation task carries its own
code + tests + comments (test-first within the task); T6 is the
cross-cutting scene-harness verification gate, T7 the documentation
slice, T8 the project-wide regression gate. Between phases, review and
update the next items' descriptions before starting them.

**Approval gate:** requested — effort is Medium scale. Recorded as a
`question (plan approval gate)` comment; `needs-producer-review` is set.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-25 — Initial plan: 8 children created, dependency edges wired,
  six automated review stages run, AC coverage review returned `proceed`
  (100 %). Review improvements: added T5→T2 dependency; added T5 AC6
  (invariant preserved under config override); added explicit
  parent-AC traceability bullets to all children. Effort/risk estimate
  refreshed.

### Appendix — planning session

No **new** clarifying questions were required in this planning session.
The three design-defining questions (Q1 global beat quantisation,
Q2 silent internal grid only, Q3 per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide
invariant) were answered by the producer during intake and are recorded
in the Appendix above, together with the producer's "all values must be
configurable" note. This plan is a mechanical decomposition of those
accepted answers — no new assumptions were introduced.

# Intake brief — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes

**Headline:** Re-base the three remaining standalone gym scenes (`GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) on the shared combat core so no production scene keeps a divergent copy of the eight combat/lifecycle methods. Use a hybrid architecture: `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`, while the two threat-free gyms consume a narrower shared base that `CombatScene` also builds on.

## Problem statement

The parent epic (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`) extracted the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) and re-based `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, deliberately leaving the three older standalone gym scenes out of scope. Those three still carry their own copies of shared method names. Because the copies are independent, a behaviour fix or feature applied to the shared core does not reach these gyms, so they can silently diverge from the shipped game and the other gyms. This item eliminates the last divergent copies.

## Users

- **Player** — expects every gym to exercise the same combat/collection code as the shipped game.
  - *As a player, I want the standalone gyms to behave the same as the shared core, so that practising in a gym reflects the real game.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one code path to change.
  - *As a developer, when I change collection, auto-fire, teleport or hit behaviour I want to change it once, so the gyms cannot drift apart.*
- **Tester** — wants the shared seams covered in one place.
  - *As a tester, I want a repo-wide guard proving the eight methods are defined once, so future duplication is caught automatically.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single shared definition of the eight methods.** Across all production scene files, each of `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` and `_readPlayerInput` is defined exactly once, in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and/or `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`). Verified by extending the existing `definesMethod` guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` to scan every production scene file repo-wide.
- [ ] **AC2 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends the shared combat core.** `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene` and no longer defines `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` or `_hitPlayer`. Its shield/phase/bomb/teleport/invulnerability behaviour is supplied through hooks (`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`, `isPlayerPhased`, `onPowerUpCollected`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` passing and a prototype-identity assertion against `CombatScene`.
- [ ] **AC3 — Threat-free gyms consume the narrower shared core.** `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` extend the narrower shared base and no longer define `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` or `_readInput`. Their per-type pickup audio and auto-fire cues are supplied through hooks (`onWeaponFired`, `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` passing plus prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC4 — Input path unified.** The private `_readInput` copies in all three gyms are removed; input mapping flows through the shared `_readPlayerInput` (covered by the AC1 guard and by the scene suites).
- [ ] **AC5 — Behaviour preserved, with two approved exceptions.** Existing gym suites pass, and the only observable behaviour changes are the two explicitly approved ones: (a) `GymPowerUpsCombat` keeps its 0.8 s post-hit invulnerability via a `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (the shared logic refactor does not change the timing), and (b) the shared teleport activation (`S` **and** `↓`) now applies in `GymPowerUpsCombat`, fixing its `S`-only implementation to match GDD §2.3. Verified by `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` suites.
- [ ] **AC6 — Shared-core validation coverage.** The newly shared seams (auto-fire cue, drop collection/cue, input mapping, and the `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook) are covered by base-class stub-subclass tests; cross-scene behavioural equivalence for the shared paths remains asserted by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4 (Module / File Breakdown) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, describing the shared base/mixin split and the hooks the standalone gyms implement.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Architecture (operator decision Q1-C):** hybrid — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` consume a narrower shared base covering drop collection + auto-fire + input, and `CombatScene` builds on that same base so there is one definition of those methods.
- **Invulnerability duration (operator decision Q2-B):** add a single overridable hook (`getInvulnerabilityDuration()`), shared default 1.5 s (game), with `GymPowerUpsCombat` overriding to 0.8 s — preserve observable timing, keep one hit-logic path.
- **Teleport activation (operator decision Q2):** adopt the shared `S`+`↓` behaviour; document as a deliberate fix of the gym's `S`-only path.
- **AC scope (operator decision Q3):** the repo-wide guard targets all eight shared method names; the private `_readInput` copies are unified onto `_readPlayerInput`. The duplicated set is 7 usages (2 + 4 + 1), not 8 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` has no `_autoFire`.
- **No full engine extraction:** spawning, wave management, HUD and menus stay scene-local; only the shared method names are consolidated.
- **Generics/type-safety:** `CombatScene` is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); the narrower base must accommodate the same generics without weakening existing type-safety.
- **Preserve public/test seams:** `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` (GymWeapons), `spawnDrop()`, `getDrops()`, `getCollectAnimations()`, `getEnemyBullets()`, `triggerTeleport()`, `getPlayerHitCount()`, `isPlayerInvulnerable()` and the shared help/back-button handles must keep working.
- **Preserve semantics:** collision radii, hit radii, collection gating (≥ 3 % scale) and the power-up lifecycles must be unchanged.
- **Minimum churn:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).

## Existing state

Confirmed by inspection (2026-09-25):

- The shared combat core exists: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` defines the eight template methods; `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` already extend it.
- The three standalone gyms still extend `Phaser.Scene` directly and define their own copies:

| File | Shared methods still defined | Line refs |
|---|---|---|
| `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` | `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 233, 418 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` | `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport`, `_hitPlayer` (plus private `_readInput`) | 423, 471, 538, 647 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` | `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 282 |

- The duplicate-body guard lives in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`definesMethod()`, regex over source). It is currently scoped to the three re-based files; its own comment notes the standalone gyms "predate the shared core" and "a repo-wide scan would flag them".
- `GymWeapons` has **no** `EffectsRegistry` (the shared `_collectDrop` requires one) and keeps its own `bullets` list. `GymPowerUpsUtility` has an `EffectsRegistry`. `GymPowerUpsCombat` has an `EffectsRegistry`, a 3-scout V-formation and its own `_hitPlayer`/`_handleTeleport` with an inline shield cycle.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability is `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8 s`; the shared `applyPlayerHit` uses `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5 s`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._handleTeleport` computes the `↓` key state but discards it (`if (!justDown) return;`), so it is `S`-only in practice.

## Desired change

1. Introduce a narrower shared base (working name `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) owning the input path (`_readPlayerInput`, cursor/WASD/handler fields), auto-fire (`_autoFire`, `spawnPlayerBullet`, `onWeaponFired`), drop collection (`_collectDrop`, `_startCollectAnimation`, `_updateCollectAnimations`, pickup cues) and the player-explosion/collect registries. Include the new `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (default 1.5 s) and the `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` hooks.
2. Refactor `CombatScene` to extend that base, keeping the combat-only template methods (`_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_handleTeleport`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`) and the enemy/bullet participant contract.
3. Re-base `GymPowerUpsCombat` on `CombatScene`: implement `getPlayer`, `getEffectsRegistry`, `getEnemyEntities` (scouts), `getEnemyBullets`/`setEnemyBullets` (scout bullets), `onPowerUpCollected` (P4 bomb notice), `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` (shield pop + short invuln), `isPlayerPhased`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` (0.8 s) and `onEnemyDestroyed`; remove the four duplicated methods and `_readInput`; use the shared collision path instead of `_handleHits`.
4. Re-base `GymWeapons` on the narrower base: give it an `EffectsRegistry`, move its bullet list to the shared `playerBullets`, implement `onWeaponFired` (from `_playShootCue`), `onWeaponCollected`/`_playPickupCue` (per-type weapon/Reset cues) and `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` seams; remove `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
5. Re-base `GymPowerUpsUtility` on the narrower base: implement `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected` for the P5/P8/P9 cues; remove `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
6. Broaden the duplicate-body guard to a repo-wide scan (or extract it to a shared test helper used by both guards).
7. Update the documentation listed under AC7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — **new**: narrower shared base (input, auto-fire, drop collection, registries, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook); `CombatScene` extends it.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — extend `CombatCoreScene`; keep the collision/teleport/hit template methods; remove the parts now owned by the narrower base.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` — base stub-subclass tests for the shared seams.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — broaden the `definesMethod` guard to a repo-wide scan; adjust identity/prototype assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — extend the narrower base; hooks for cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`; keep public test seams.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — extend `CombatScene`; implement participant accessors and hooks; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — extend the narrower base; hook for pickup cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — verify behaviour preserved and public test seams unchanged.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — describe the shared base/mixin split and hooks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hybrid split ambiguity.** Deciding which methods belong to the narrower base vs `CombatScene` can sprawl. Mitigation: keep the narrower base to input + auto-fire + drop collection + registries; anything collision/teleport/hit-specific stays in `CombatScene`.

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.

- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.

# Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

## Goal
Provide the single shared entry point `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)`
that composes every juice layer (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst,
flash, debris, shockwave) so no scene has to know the layer set, and returns the
handles/registry so teardown can destroy everything.

## User story
As a developer, I call one function with a position and severity and the full
player-death effect plays; each layer is tunable/toggleable in one module and I
cannot accidentally play two sounds or two particle bursts.

## Scope
- `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)` in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`:
  - resolves params via `resolveJuiceParams`;
  - plays `playPlayerDestructionSound()` exactly once;

- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using the scene harness plus spies on the audio module and `spawnExplosionParticles`.

- The generic `playDestructionSound()` must NOT be called by this helper.

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer was implemented in AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts) but is a standalone pure-core library: nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition for a run is still hard-coded in src/waves/Formations.ts (the LEVELS constant), and PlayScene drives those static definitions through WaveManager.

This work item wires the sequencer into the actual playable run so that wave composition is **generated at runtime** from a target difficulty curve, rather than being fixed. This is the in-game integration counterpart to AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL (the Dev Utilities gym scene), which provides a designer-facing preview but does not affect the game.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Relationship

- Builds on the sequencer delivered by AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X (in_review; code already committed to dev).
- Sibling of AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL (gym preview scene) — that item is a designer tool; this item is the real game integration. Neither blocks the other.
- The static LEVELS definitions remain the source of level names, boss handling, and the fallback path.

## Goal / user story

As a player, enemy waves should be generated to follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly, instead of every playthrough using the same fixed enemy counts.

As a designer, I want to control that curve from configuration so I can tune the difficulty ramp without editing Formations.ts.

## Scope

1. **Curve source** — define where the target difficulty curve comes from. Provide a baked-in default curve (per-level/per-wave targets on the 0–100 scale) and allow it to be overridden from configuration (config store / settings), consistent with how other tunables are persisted.
2. **Runtime generation** — at run start, build the curve plus a candidate pool (defaultCandidatePool() or the config-store archetypes) and call sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts.
3. **Conversion** — convert each ShootableWave into a WaveDefinition (groups / shootEnabled) that WaveManager can consume. AdjustedGroup already extends WaveGroup, so this is a structural mapping.
4. **Injection** — allow WaveManager to be driven by the generated level/wave definitions while defaulting to the static LEVELS, so existing behaviour and tests are preserved.
5. **Campaign rules** — honour the GDD §2.4/§2.5 rule: Levels 1–3 do not fire, Levels 4–5 do (drive shootEnabled, e.g. via the sequencer's defaultShootEnabled option).
6. **Fallback** — if the sequencer produces no usable groups, fall back to the static LEVELS without crashing.
7. **Determinism** — the same curve plus candidate pool must produce the same waves (the sequencer is already deterministic; the wiring must not introduce non-determinism).

## Out of scope

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting the curve based on player performance).
- Editing the difficulty curve at runtime through a UI (that is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).
- Replacing boss / asteroid spawning logic.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — WaveManager can be driven by generated LevelDefinition/WaveDefinition data; when no override is supplied it uses the static LEVELS exactly as today (existing WaveManager tests still pass unchanged).
2. **Runtime generation runs** — at run start the game calls sequencer() with a difficulty curve and candidate pool and obtains a SequencerResult.
3. **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what PlayScene spawns (verifiable via the spawn plan or a test harness), not the static LEVELS.
4. **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
5. **Campaign fire rule** — for Levels 1–3 shootEnabled is false; for Levels 4–5 it is true (test asserts both).
6. **Determinism** — calling the generation twice with the same curve and pool yields identical waves.
7. **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve or candidate pool falls back to the static LEVELS and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
8. **No regressions** — the full test suite passes (npm test).

## Key files

- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — existing sequencer (read-only; call site)
- src/waves/WaveManager.ts — allow injected level/wave definitions
- src/waves/Formations.ts — static LEVELS, fallback and level metadata
- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts — drive the generated waves
- src/core/configStore.ts / src/core/configTypes.ts — where a curve override could live
- **New:** a small module to build the curve/pool and convert SequencerResult into LevelDefinition[] (e.g. src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts) plus its tests

## Design decisions to confirm at intake

- Does the generated curve **replace** LEVELS entirely, or is the sequencer behind a feature flag / config toggle with static levels as the default?
- Per-level curves versus a single run-length curve (5 levels × N waves).
- Where the curve is persisted (config store versus a dedicated bundled default).
